To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the membrane alterations in health and diseases, with particular reference, to immune function and cancers, may be caused by binding of toxicants with membrane receptors and the subsequent transmission of message to the genomic material for altered DNA, protein synthesis, cell division and ultimately cancer.
membrane receptors bind with the ligands, transmit a message to the nucleus, the message is processed by the DNA/RNA/protein synthesis, which ultimately alters the cell function.
the binding of toxicants to the cell membrane receptors may alter the normal function of the immune system, and may cause genetic alterations, leading to the development of cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of membrane receptors of the immune cells, and their binding with various environmental toxicants, which are responsible for the altered immune function and predisposition to cancer.
membrane binding, membrane alteration, immune response and cancer.
the elucidation of molecular mechanism of membrane alterations in health and diseases with particular reference to immunosuppression and carcinogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cell membrane is the most important and vital structure of the cell, and any alteration of its structure and function may lead to a disease process.
the membrane alterations in health and diseases, particularly immune function and cancer, are inter-related and the membrane alterations are the common denominator of the pathogenesis.
the membrane alterations are the most common phenomena in health and disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the membrane alterations, in health or disease, are a result of the interaction of toxicants with the membrane, followed by a cascade of biochemical and molecular events which ultimately lead to the development of a disease.
membrane alterations are the cause of all disorders including cancer, and membrane binding is an initial event in the development of cancer.
the cell membrane is an important biological barrier and its alteration may be the primary event for the initiation of the disease process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the membrane is the first target of toxicants, and the damage caused by the toxicants is transmitted to the biomolecular structures, and ultimately leads to a disorder or disease.
the membrane plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of disease, and the membrane alteration is an early event in the development of the disease.
the cell membrane plays a pivotal role in maintaining the health of the host and its alteration leads to the development of disease.
